analysis: Integration pass over the SSD eviction refactor (T-041, TB-007, A-001). Replayed source now shows the previously unseen helper SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift, new lines ~11-34). It resolves the earlier open questions: it probes index.oldest(), calls the store's retire closure, returns 0 on externalChange, returns on the first positive indexedBytesFreed, and otherwise iterates a single oldestFirstSnapshot() (fixed copy, so bounded) while skipping the first tag. This preserves the prior semantics that a busy or undeletable victim does not pin newer victims, and that external loss hands control back to the disk budget. Both stores (SSDPrefixCache.swift ~1771-1778, SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift 13-19) still delete only via retireIndexedEntries, so removalLock, hasSafeRoot/ownsEvictionRoot, no-follow removal, file leases and the epoch barrier are unchanged. Paths derive from HMAC tags, not caller input, so no traversal surface. SSDBlockIndex.swift 167-225 replaces the sort with a copy-then-min-heap snapshot; the ordering (lastAccess, then lexicographic tag) matches oldest(), tags are unique so the order is total, and the heap sift logic is correct. The index lock covers only the copy, and retirement runs outside it. Stats accounting is preserved. Docs (prefix-cache.md, ssd-kv-cache.md) and the changelog accurately describe this and make no claim that eviction purges detached media or rotates the epoch. TTL (1800 s), HMAC lookup tags, DBK3 crypto, cacheSalt scoping, disk-budget values and KEK-wipe purge are untouched, so the T-041 mitigations hold. Residual: the retireIndexedEntries internals and the new tests were examined only through patch excerpts and summaries; one replay scope was incomplete (38 omitted units). A concurrent-schedule nuance (victim chosen from a pre-attempt snapshot) affects ordering only, not confidentiality. No security regression identified.
